title: Types of bonds in India
objectives: Name the main bond types in India and their key point for clients.
Explain why a PSU bond is not a government guarantee, and why AT1 is high risk.
body_md:
G-secs are long-term central-government bonds: virtually no default risk, still interest-rate risk. T-bills are short-term government borrowing (91, 182 or 364 days), issued at a discount with no coupon. SDLs are state-government bonds, usually yielding a little more than a G-sec. PSU bonds are often AAA but are not the same as a government guarantee. Corporate bonds/NCDs pay higher yield for higher credit risk — check the rating. Tax-free bonds (mostly old PSU issues) trade only on the exchange now. Zero-coupon bonds pay no interest and are bought at a discount. Floating-rate bonds reset their coupon with a benchmark. 54EC bonds save tax on long-term capital gains from property, with a 5-year lock-in. Perpetual/AT1 bonds have no maturity and can be written off.

| Type | What it is | Key point for clients |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G-sec (Government security) | Long-term bond issued by the central government | Virtually no default risk; still has interest-rate risk |
| T-bill (Treasury bill) | Short-term government borrowing: 91, 182 or 364 days | Issued at a discount, repaid at face value; no coupon |
| SDL (State Development Loan) | Bond issued by a state government | Usually yields a little more than a G-sec |
| PSU bond | Issued by a public sector company | Often AAA; not the same as a government guarantee |
| Corporate bond / NCD | Issued by a company; NCD = non-convertible debenture | Higher yield = higher credit risk; check the rating |
| Tax-free bond | Interest exempt from tax; mostly issued by PSUs in the past | Available only on the exchange now; check liquidity |
| Zero-coupon bond | No interest paid; bought at a discount, repaid at face value | All return comes at maturity |
| Floating-rate bond | Coupon resets with a benchmark rate | Less interest-rate risk |
| 54EC bond | Capital gains bonds from specified issuers, 5-year lock-in | Used to save tax on long-term capital gains from property; confirm eligibility with a CA |
| Perpetual / AT1 bond | No maturity date; banks use them as capital | High risk: can be written off (see Niche topics) |
example: A T-bill bought at a discount is repaid at face value; a 54EC bond is used after selling property — confirm eligibility with a CA.
say: PSU bonds are often AAA, but that is not a government guarantee.
AT1 bonds can be written off; they are not a fixed deposit substitute.
never: A PSU bond is guaranteed by the government.
AT1 bonds are as safe as FDs.
